walkthrough:
Express $x^2$ in terms of $y$ from the curve equation $y = x^2 - 1$:
$$x^2 = y + 1$$

Set up the volume of revolution integral for rotation through $360^\circ$ about the $y$-axis from $y = 0$ to $y = h$:
$$V = \pi \int_0^h x^2\,dy = \pi \int_0^h (y + 1)\,dy$$

Integrate and apply limits:
$$V = \pi \left[ \frac{1}{2}y^2 + y \right]_0^h = \pi \left(\frac{1}{2}h^2 + h - 0\right) = \pi\left(\frac{1}{2}h^2 + h\right)$$

Set up the integral for the area bounded between the curve and the $y$-axis from $y = 0$ to $y = 3$:
$$\text{Area} = \int_0^3 x\,dy = \int_0^3 \sqrt{y + 1}\,dy = \int_0^3 (y + 1)^{\frac{1}{2}}\,dy$$

Integrate using the reverse chain rule:
$$\text{Area} = \left[ \frac{(y + 1)^{\frac{3}{2}}}{\frac{3}{2}} \right]_0^3 = \left[ \frac{2}{3}(y + 1)^{\frac{3}{2}} \right]_0^3$$

Evaluate at the upper limit $y = 3$ and lower limit $y = 0$:
$$\text{Area} = \frac{2}{3}(3 + 1)^{\frac{3}{2}} - \frac{2}{3}(0 + 1)^{\frac{3}{2}} = \frac{2}{3}(4^{\frac{3}{2}}) - \frac{2}{3}(1^{\frac{3}{2}}) = \frac{2}{3}(8) - \frac{2}{3}(1) = \frac{14}{3} \quad \left(= 4\frac{2}{3}\right)$$

Differentiate the volume formula with respect to $h$:
$$\frac{dV}{dh} = \frac{d}{dh}\left[\pi\left(\frac{1}{2}h^2 + h\right)\right] = \pi(h + 1)$$

Apply the chain rule for connected rates of change with $\frac{dV}{dt} = 2\text{ cm}^3\text{ s}^{-1}$:
$$\frac{dh}{dt} = \frac{dV}{dt} \div \frac{dV}{dh} = \frac{2}{4\pi} = \frac{1}{2\pi}\text{ cm s}^{-1} \quad (\approx 0.159\text{ cm s}^{-1})$$
